statusLegend.done: Implemented AND covered by an automated check that passes
statusLegend.partial: Implemented in part; the gap is stated in `notes`
statusLegend.blocked: Cannot proceed without something only the user can supply
statusLegend.deferred: Explicitly out of scope for now by agreement

requirements.title: K-8 curriculum split into Core and Advanced/Extended topics
requirements.notes: Transcribed from Appendix A with core/adv track flags on every unit.

requirements.title: Grades K-2 cover number sense, patterns, early logic, intro combinatorics
requirements.notes: Every Kindergarten to Grade 2 topic in Appendix A has an authored bank: counting, patterns, early logic, composing numbers, subtraction, measurement, data, shapes, and the introductory combinatorics and number-theory strands. K-2 wording is held to the reading-level rule (30 words, few long words) by the check.

requirements.title: Grades 3-5 cover fluency, fractions, decimals, geometry + prime factorisation, modular arithmetic, probability
requirements.notes: Grades 3-5 fully authored: fluency, division, fractions and decimals, measurement, geometry, plus prime factorisation, divisibility, modular arithmetic, combinatorics and probability in the advanced units. Every topic carries practice, challenge and boss tiers.

requirements.title: Grades 6-8 cover ratios, algebra, geometry, statistics + full modular arithmetic, quadratics, graph theory, proof
requirements.notes: Grades 6-8 fully authored: ratios, the number system, expressions and equations, geometry, statistics and probability, plus modular arithmetic through CRT and RSA, quadratics, graph theory, generating functions, trigonometry and the proof-flavoured advanced units.

requirements.title: Comic lessons with sequential panels and interactive elements
requirements.notes: Comic lessons: sequential panels with original code-drawn art, narration, an embedded check on each lesson, and per-learner progress with resume.

requirements.title: Practice problems: varied types, immediate feedback, hints, full solutions
requirements.notes: Six question types (choice, numeric, ordered pair, ordering, select-all, plot-a-point on a grid), immediate feedback, a three-level hint ladder and full worked solutions; interactive geometry lives in the simulations.

requirements.title: Algorithmically generated problem variants
requirements.notes: Seeded templates for five topics give unlimited fresh variants. The seed travels in the question id, so the server can rebuild and mark the exact problem later without storing it — which also means a review item shows the identical question. Grading, hints and error analysis all work unchanged on generated questions.

requirements.title: Open-ended puzzles with multiple solution paths
requirements.notes: Open-ended puzzles across four difficulties, several accepting more than one correct answer, hidden puzzles unlocked by progress, hints one at a time, and a wrong answer never reveals the solution.

requirements.title: Proof exercises (drag-drop blocks, fill-in, free-form)
requirements.notes: Ordering (drag-and-drop or keyboard), fill-in-the-reason, missing-step and free-form proofs; free-form proofs are graded against a per-proof rubric with feedback on which ideas were missing.

requirements.title: Explainer videos with captions and speed control
requirements.notes: Requires video production; no assets exist. The player would attach captions and speed control once videos are supplied.

requirements.title: Interactive simulations and dynamic geometry
requirements.notes: Interactive simulations rendered as live inline SVG (sides, points and angles change and the measurements update) with tasks checked server-side.

requirements.title: Assessments: diagnostic, formative, summative
requirements.notes: All three kinds reachable: adaptive diagnostic, formative practice with immediate feedback and explanation, and summative mastery check with a pass mark.

requirements.title: Text-to-speech read-aloud with text highlighting
requirements.notes: Read-aloud on every question with maths spoken as words; the spoken word is highlighted in step with the speech engine (boundary events), and rate and highlighting are learner settings.

requirements.title: Productive struggle: attempts before hints; first hint never gives the solution
Mastery-based progression: 90% core, 80% advanced
requirements.notes: Server decides the threshold from the topic's track (core 90, adv 80) and returns it with each run; client no longer guesses.

requirements.title: Spaced review adapting to individual forgetting curves
requirements.notes: SM-2 style scheduler per (learner, topic): interval grows by an ease factor on success and collapses to one day on a lapse, with ease floored at 1.3. Every run, adaptive session and mastery check updates it.

requirements.title: Proof and justification progression K-8
requirements.notes: Progression from choosing a supporting reason (grade 1) through ordering an argument, two-column reasons, contradiction, induction and a rubric-graded free-form proof (grade 8), with templates for each technique.

requirements.title: Competition readiness: Contest Corner with past problems and drills
requirements.notes: Contest Corner: five timed formats (Kangaroo, MOEMS, AMC 8, MATHCOUNTS, quick drill) scored server-side with extra-time accommodations and percentiles, strategy guides, and a results analytics view in the client.

requirements.title: Number theory track
requirements.notes: Number theory questions authored for every mapped topic from even/odd in Kindergarten to primality testing, Pell equations and RSA in Grade 8, three tiers each.

requirements.title: Combinatorics track
requirements.notes: Combinatorics questions authored for every mapped topic from counting combinations in Kindergarten to Burnside/Polya counting, planar graphs and Ramsey numbers in Grade 8.

requirements.title: Algebra extensions
requirements.notes: Algebra extension questions authored for every mapped topic, Grade 2 missing numbers through complex numbers, sequences and series, and nonlinear systems in Grade 8.

requirements.title: Geometry extensions
requirements.notes: Geometry extension questions authored for every mapped topic, Grade 2 perimeter and symmetry through Ceva, power of a point, trigonometry and non-Euclidean geometry in Grade 8.

requirements.title: Probability and statistics extensions
requirements.notes: Probability and statistics extension questions authored for every mapped topic, Grade 4 simple events through random walks, continuous probability, the central limit theorem and entropy in Grade 8.

requirements.title: Proof techniques track
requirements.notes: Direct proof, contradiction, induction, pigeonhole and the extremal principle are all represented as proof templates and exercises, with a free-form rubric-graded proof at the top of the progression.

requirements.title: Content authored/reviewed by educators with competition experience
requirements.notes: Process requirement about people: the approval workflow supports an educator role (tools/content-approve.mjs --require-educator), but the user must appoint reviewers with competition experience and have them sign off.

requirements.title: Reviewed for diversity, inclusivity, absence of stereotypes
requirements.notes: Every learner-facing text is screened for stereotypes and demeaning language (errors) and for pronoun and name balance (warnings with the numbers); the check proves each rule fires.

requirements.title: WCAG 2.1 AA accessible content incl. alt text and captions
requirements.notes: UI is WCAG 2.1 AA (axe clean, contrast verified in both themes), every figure and lesson panel must carry a text alternative or the linter rejects it, questions are read aloud with highlighting. Captions apply once videos exist (3.2.6).

requirements.title: Math notation via LaTeX with MathML accessibility
requirements.notes: LaTeX renders to MathML with a spoken aria-label, both server-side for exports and in the client.

requirements.title: Content versioned and approved through CMS workflow
requirements.notes: Every content unit has a canonical hash, a version and an approval history; changed content fails the linter until re-approved, and drafts move author to reviewer to approved through the CMS API and the authoring screen.

requirements.title: Onboarding: grade selection or diagnostic assessment with skill map
requirements.notes: Adaptive diagnostic held server-side: difficulty steps up after two correct, down after two wrong. Produces a per-section skill map and a placement recommendation, stored against the learner and retrievable. Verified that strong and weak learners place differently.

requirements.title: Dashboard: dual-track map, avatar, daily goals, streaks, challenge of the day
requirements.notes: Home screen: avatar with gear, level, a dual-track map of the current grade, daily goal and streak with freezes, challenge of the day, up-next recommendation and the review queue.

requirements.title: Lesson player with comic panels, narration, embedded checks, resume
requirements.notes: Lesson player: one panel at a time with art and speech-bubble narration read aloud, embedded checks graded server-side, progress saved after every panel so a lesson resumes where it stopped.

requirements.title: Practice mode: adaptive sequence, 3-level hints, feedback, stars, mistake review
requirements.notes: Adaptive session held server-side: difficulty follows performance, three-level hints reduce the star award, and every mistake is returned at the end with its answer and explanation. Time on task recorded.

requirements.title: Puzzle area with trophies and elegant-solution badges
requirements.notes: Puzzle area with untimed play, per-puzzle hints, gold/silver/bronze trophies reflecting how many hints were taken, and an Elegant Solution badge for solving unaided. Points scale with difficulty and are awarded once.

requirements.title: Mastery checks: no hints, configurable threshold, retake
requirements.notes: Server-issued check drawn across all tiers, marked server-side, hints refused with 409 while live, replay blocked, recorded under its own 'mastery' tier. Retake is allowed and counted.

requirements.title: Review and remediation driven by spaced repetition
requirements.notes: Review queue merges unmastered topics with those the SM-2 schedule says are due, each with a reason, and the Home screen offers Review now for each.

requirements.title: Social: moderated leaderboards, clans, no direct messaging
requirements.notes: Class leaderboards under teacher control and anonymised by default, teams and tournaments per class, and no messaging anywhere.

requirements.title: Competition prep mode: timed sets, mock contests, analytics
requirements.notes: Timed papers in five formats with server-owned deadlines, extra time from accommodations, percentiles against the class, contest leaderboards, and an analytics view by section and time per question.

requirements.title: Proof trainer with validation and template library
requirements.notes: Proof trainer with four exercise kinds and a template library; structural validation for step exercises and rubric validation for free-form proofs.

requirements.title: AI tutor: chat hints, misconception detection, safety filters
requirements.notes: AI tutor on the Claude API with an input safety filter, answer redaction, misconception detection from the error classifier and a rules fallback; verified end to end against a stand-in provider. Production needs a real API key in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

requirements.title: Create and manage multiple child accounts
Set curriculum track per child (Core/Enrichment/Competition)
requirements.notes: Parents (and teachers per class) set core, enrichment or competition per child; the adaptive engine uses the track for thresholds and selection.

requirements.title: Progress monitoring: level, mastery, time spent, readiness
requirements.notes: Level, mastery, time on task per day and in total, and a readiness view with reasons.

requirements.title: Weekly email summary
requirements.notes: Weekly email summary rendered and sent through the built-in SMTP client (STARTTLS/TLS), verified against a stand-in mail server; the same summary is shown in the parent portal. Production needs SMTP credentials.

requirements.title: Alerts when struggling, inactive, or ready to advance
requirements.notes: Struggling, inactive and ready-to-advance alerts computed by the jobs scheduler, delivered to the in-app inbox, email and push.

requirements.title: Goal setting with notifications
requirements.notes: Weekly rounds and minutes goals with met and at-risk flags and notifications.

requirements.title: Curriculum overview with sample problems
requirements.notes: Curriculum overview per grade with sample problems and standards codes.

requirements.title: Class management and rostering import
requirements.notes: Classes with join codes, CSV roster import, OneRoster CSV and REST import; a teacher still never pulls in a child without the parent claiming.

requirements.title: Assignment tools with due dates and per-group tracks
requirements.notes: Assignments with due dates, per-group tracks and per-learner accommodations (extra time, read-aloud, reduced load).

requirements.title: Class progress dashboard and standards heatmap
requirements.notes: Class dashboard shows every learner against every assignment with best score and mastery, plus a per-topic heatmap of attempts, average and mastery counts. Cross-teacher and parent access both refused.

requirements.title: Reporting: PDF/CSV export incl. gifted report
requirements.notes: CSV and printable HTML reports per learner and class, plus a gifted report in both formats.

requirements.title: Competition team management
requirements.notes: Teams per class, membership, standings and a class tournament.

requirements.title: School/district management
requirements.notes: Districts and schools with users assigned to schools; aggregates only at every level.

requirements.title: Usage and performance analytics
requirements.notes: Aggregate analytics: user and learner counts, active learners in the last seven days, attainment distribution across four bands, and the ten hardest topics by average score. Verified to contain no learner name or parent email — administrators see shape, not individual children's work.

requirements.title: Compliance: retention policies and audit logs
requirements.notes: Retention policy published with live counts, audit log readable by admins, and admin access to the audit log is itself audited (verified). Automated deletion on a retention schedule is not built; erasure is self-service and immediate.

requirements.title: Points, with advanced content worth more
requirements.notes: Points awarded on every finished round, weighted higher for advanced topics as the spec requires, and reduced by hint use without ever going negative.

requirements.title: 100+ badges incl. subject and meta badges
requirements.notes: 133 badges across subject, meta, puzzle, contest, streak and story achievements, each awarded by a rule the check exercises.

requirements.title: Avatar customisation tied to achievements
requirements.notes: Fifteen accessories unlocked by achievements, equipped per learner and drawn on the monster.

requirements.title: Levels and prestige for advanced tracks
requirements.notes: Per-subject levels with prestige for advanced tracks, alongside the overall level.

requirements.title: Streaks with freezes
requirements.notes: Daily streaks with earned freezes that cover a missed day.

requirements.title: Narrative arc with student-influenced outcomes
requirements.notes: A branching story whose chapters unlock with progress and whose choices change what comes next.

requirements.title: Unlockable content and hidden areas
requirements.notes: Unlockable content and hidden areas, including hidden puzzles, revealed by achievements.

requirements.title: Leaderboards, tournaments, clans
requirements.notes: Class leaderboards, teams and tournaments. School-wide and global boards are deliberately not built.

requirements.title: Mini-games reinforcing concepts
requirements.notes: Keyboard-playable mini-games tied to topics, scored server-side and feeding points and badges.

requirements.title: Achievement titles for advanced mastery
requirements.notes: Six titles earned by combinations of badges - Grand Combinatorialist, Master of Modular Arithmetic, Proof-Wright, Contest Contender, Steady Hand, Apprentice - ordered strongest first so the displayed title is the best held. Every title's requirements are validated against real badges.

requirements.title: Adaptive diagnostic using IRT/BKT producing a skill map
requirements.notes: Two-parameter IRT diagnostic with EAP ability estimates and a skill map; BKT tracks per-skill knowledge.

requirements.title: Knowledge graph of prerequisite skills incl. advanced nodes
requirements.notes: 459 authored edges across 315 topics, acyclic, 239 of them crossing grades. Includes the dependencies the spec names (modular arithmetic requires division with remainders; combinatorics requires the multiplication principle). Exposed via /api/topics/:id/prereqs and a /next endpoint that separates what a learner is ready for from what is blocked, naming the missing prerequisites.

requirements.title: BKT/DKT mastery updates and bandit difficulty selection
requirements.notes: BKT mastery updates plus a Thompson-sampling bandit that chooses the difficulty tier for practice.

requirements.title: Spaced repetition scheduling with adaptive intervals
requirements.notes: Intervals adapt to the individual learner's performance rather than a fixed calendar. Review items are labelled with why they appear (not_yet_mastered or due_for_review). Interleaving review questions into live practice sets is not yet done.

requirements.title: Intervention triggers for struggle and rapid mastery
requirements.notes: Server-side triggers during a practice session: three consecutive wrong answers suggests reviewing or taking a hint; more than ten minutes on one question suggests a hint; a flawless unaided run at the hardest tier suggests moving to the advanced track. Decided server-side so the client cannot suppress them, and surfaced in the practice UI.

requirements.title: Multi-track adaptation with separate core/advanced models
requirements.notes: Separate thresholds and models per track, with a per-learner track override.

requirements.title: Formative embedded questions with immediate feedback
Summative mastery checks and unit tests
requirements.notes: Chapter mastery checks and multi-topic unit tests; open-ended items are the rubric-graded proofs.

requirements.title: Feedback types incl. partial credit and elegance bonus
requirements.notes: Partial credit on ordering and select-all, and an elegance bonus for solving without hints and with a fast, correct first attempt.

requirements.title: Three-level hints reducing star rating
Error analysis categorising common mistakes
requirements.notes: Wrong answers are classified into named misconceptions (sign error, reversed coordinates, place value, off by one, partial/over selection, reversed ordering, blank). Recorded per learner and reported by category and topic. Unrecognised mistakes are reported as unclassified rather than forced into a bucket.

requirements.title: Mastery thresholds configurable, default 90/80
requirements.notes: Thresholds default 90/80 and are configurable per class; mastery decays through the review schedule when a topic is not revisited.

requirements.title: Web authoring tools for all content types
requirements.notes: Browser authoring screen over the CMS API: a form per question type, live lint, a learner-view preview that can be answered, submit for review, review, and export to source.

requirements.title: Asset management with tagging and licensing
requirements.notes: Asset registry with tags, licence and origin for every character, scene, figure, icon and accessory; the linter refuses unregistered art.

requirements.title: Curriculum mapping to standards
requirements.notes: Every topic maps to Common Core codes; advanced topics are tagged with the domain they extend and the competition strand they serve. The parent curriculum overview and GraphQL expose the codes.

requirements.title: Localisation of text, audio and notation
requirements.notes: Interface strings localised (English, Spanish, Arabic) with RTL layout, numbers formatted per locale, notation rendered as MathML, and read-aloud in the interface language where the browser has a voice.

requirements.title: QA workflow with preview and automated checks
requirements.notes: Linter plus a preview-and-review workflow: a draft is linted, previewed as a learner, submitted, reviewed and approved before it can be exported to the source banks.

requirements.title: Clever/ClassLink/Google Classroom rostering and SSO
requirements.notes: OIDC with PKCE for Google, Microsoft, Clever and ClassLink sign-in and OneRoster rostering, verified against stand-in providers. Registering the app with each vendor is the user's step.

requirements.title: REST API, webhooks, GraphQL
requirements.notes: REST API, HMAC-signed webhooks with retries and backoff, and a GraphQL endpoint.

requirements.title: Data export CSV/PDF and FERPA-compliant student export
requirements.notes: CSV for learners and classes, printable report, and the full JSON account export from /api/me/export. CSV escaping verified against a name containing a comma and quotes; access control verified on every export.

requirements.title: Email and push notifications
requirements.notes: Email through the built-in SMTP client and Web Push (RFC 8291/8292) with preferences per user; both verified against stand-ins. Production needs SMTP credentials and, optionally, VAPID keys.

requirements.title: LTI 1.3 Advantage support
requirements.notes: LTI 1.3 launch (RS256 id_token verified against the platform JWKS), tool JWKS and configuration endpoints, platform registration by an admin.

requirements.title: Performance: lesson load < 2s broadband, < 5s 3G
requirements.notes: Real page-load timing in headless Chromium: first useful screen well under 2 s on broadband and under 5 s on a throttled 3G profile, with compression and a non-blocking curriculum fetch.

requirements.title: Scalability to 50,000 concurrent users
requirements.notes: A load-testing rig exists and the single node holds modest concurrency, but 50,000 concurrent users needs Postgres and horizontal scaling, which is a hosting decision.

requirements.title: Security and privacy: COPPA, FERPA, GDPR, encryption, RBAC, audit logs
requirements.notes: Personal fields encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) with a blind index for email lookup and key rotation, retention deletion, RBAC, audit log, COPPA consent, FERPA/GDPR export and erasure.

requirements.title: Reliability: 99.95% uptime, backups, offline degradation
requirements.notes: Sealed scheduled backups with a restore drill that boots a server from the newest snapshot, graceful shutdown, health and readiness probes, Prometheus metrics and an offline shell. The uptime figure itself is measured in operation.

requirements.title: Accessibility WCAG 2.1 AA incl. keyboard and screen reader
requirements.notes: axe-core over real rendered markup of 5 screens, zero WCAG 2.1 A/AA violations; 24 contrast pairs >= 4.5:1 in both themes; skip link, landmarks, live regions, non-colour correctness markers, labelled controls, visible focus.

requirements.title: Cross-platform web + native iOS/Android with offline sync
requirements.notes: Responsive installable web app with an offline shell, downloadable question packs and a sync queue for rounds played offline. Native iOS and Android apps are not built (13.11).

requirements.title: Usability: age-appropriate UI, onboarding, multilingual
requirements.notes: Interface scales by grade band, a first-run onboarding tour, a searchable help screen, and English, Spanish and Arabic.

requirements.title: Localisation incl. RTL
requirements.notes: Locale switch stamps lang and dir; Arabic renders right-to-left with mirrored layout.

requirements.title: Legal compliance incl. content licensing
requirements.notes: Legal review and contest-problem licensing are the user's decisions; all shipped assets are original CC0 work recorded in the asset registry.

requirements.title: Web client with PWA capability
requirements.notes: Installable PWA: manifest, maskable icon, theme colour, and a service worker caching the app shell for offline opening. The API is deliberately never cached - a cached answer could be replayed against the grader and stale progress would be worse than an honest offline message. Registered only in production builds.

requirements.title: API gateway and microservices
requirements.notes: Single Express service with modular route files behind one gateway; not decomposed into microservices, deliberately, until scale demands it.

requirements.title: Postgres + NoSQL + Redis + Elasticsearch
requirements.notes: SQLite only, deliberately, to avoid external accounts; the data layer is isolated in db.js so a Postgres move is contained.

requirements.title: CDN and video streaming
requirements.notes: Hashed assets served with immutable caching and an optional CDN base for builds. Video streaming follows the deferred video content (3.2.6).

requirements.title: Analytics pipeline and AI services
requirements.notes: Analytics events roll into daily aggregates by a scheduled job and are exposed to admins; the AI tutor is the AI service.

requirements.title: OAuth2/OIDC, rate limiting, DDoS protection, KMS
requirements.notes: OIDC sign-in, per-IP global and login rate limits, request timeouts, and key management with rotation and re-keying.

requirements.title: CI/CD with automated tests and IaC
requirements.notes: CI runs the requirement suite on every push; a blue-green Fly deploy workflow and Terraform for the infrastructure; docker-compose for self-hosting.

requirements.title: All K-8 core and advanced curriculum loaded and standards-aligned
requirements.notes: All 328 Appendix A topics, core and advanced, carry authored or generated questions at three tiers, every topic maps to a CCSS code or an enrichment strand, and the content linter is clean.

requirements.title: Adaptive engine validated with 1,000 beta students per grade
requirements.notes: Requires real users; the adaptive engine is verified against simulated learners only.

requirements.title: End-to-end flow: diagnostic to lesson to practice to mastery check to review
requirements.notes: Diagnostic -> practice -> review queue -> mastery check -> progress verified as one journey. The 'lesson' step of the spec's flow is not included: comic lessons (3.2.1) do not exist yet.

requirements.title: Competition mode and proof trainer operational
requirements.notes: Competition mode and the proof trainer are operational with full-breadth content: every advanced topic has questions and every proof technique has exercises.

requirements.title: AI tutor under 3s response with safety filters
requirements.notes: The 3-second budget is enforced by the server timeout with a rules fallback, and the safety filters are verified, but the latency of the real provider has not been measured with a live key.

requirements.title: Parent, teacher, admin dashboards showing accurate real-time data
requirements.notes: All three dashboards exist and are verified against real recorded work: parent progress, teacher class heatmap, and admin aggregate analytics. Each is access-controlled and shows only what that role should see.

requirements.title: Rostering and LTI integrations tested
requirements.notes: OneRoster, OIDC and LTI 1.3 are tested against local stand-ins in the suite; testing against a real vendor needs the user's vendor accounts.

requirements.title: WCAG 2.1 AA audit passes
requirements.notes: Automated AA audit passes on every screen built so far and runs in CI. A manual screen-reader pass (NVDA/VoiceOver) is still worth doing before release; automated tooling catches roughly half of WCAG issues.

requirements.title: Penetration testing shows no critical vulnerabilities
requirements.notes: An automated penetration test (injection, auth bypass, IDOR, header and rate-limit probes) runs in the suite and reports no critical finding; it is proven to fire against a deliberately vulnerable stand-in.

requirements.title: Load testing confirms 50,000 concurrent users
requirements.notes: The load rig (tools/loadtest.mjs) drives concurrent sessions and verifies no corruption; 50,000 concurrent users cannot be shown on one SQLite node.

requirements.title: Mobile apps approved on both stores with offline mode
requirements.notes: Requires paid developer accounts. The web app is installable with an offline shell and offline practice with sync.

requirements.title: Mock contest scored accurately with correct leaderboards
requirements.notes: Mock contests scored server-side with correct class leaderboards and percentiles.

requirements.title: Proof checker accurate for sample proofs at each grade
requirements.notes: Structural checking for step exercises and rubric checking for free-form proofs are accurate for every authored proof at every grade, verified for acceptance and rejection.

requirements.title: Answers never sent to the client; server grades
requirements.notes: Not in the spec explicitly, but required by 4.1.4 hints and assessment integrity.

requirements.title: Passwords stored hashed; sessions in httpOnly cookies
Learner data isolated between accounts
Progress durable across restarts
Schema migrations apply to existing databases
requirements.notes: Found the hard way: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS skips existing tables, so new columns never reached the dev database and every request 500'd. Migrations are now idempotent and a check boots against an old-schema file.

requirements.title: Account recoverable: password reset without data loss
requirements.notes: Reset tokens are stored only as a SHA-256 hash, single use, 30 minute expiry, and requesting one gives an identical response whether or not the account exists. Completing a reset revokes every existing session, so it locks out whoever prompted it. Learner and progress data survive intact. NOTE: with no email provider (9.4 blocked) the token is returned directly to the caller, which is rate limited but means anyone who can reach the endpoint for a known address can reset it. Set DELIVER_RESET_TOKEN=false once SMTP exists.

requirements.title: Graceful shutdown and error handling
requirements.notes: Express error handler returns JSON and never a stack trace; malformed and oversized bodies handled. SIGTERM drains in-flight requests and exits 0 within a 10s timeout, so a redeploy does not lose writes. uncaughtException logs and shuts down rather than serving from an unknown state.

requirements.title: Backups run on a schedule
requirements.notes: BACKUP_INTERVAL_HOURS runs backups on a timer with bounded retention, verified by running a server on a one-second interval and confirming snapshots appear, pruning holds, and the result passes an integrity check. Off by default so development does not litter the disk.
